Indian Trust Fund, Revenue: Asking for List of Leases

(Previous correspondence on page 1 - 221, Report for 1923 - 24)

AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, May 9, 1925.

SIR, - I beg to draw your attention to my letter of April 9th, 1924, in which I requested to be furnished with a list, of
all leases of Indian lands in force on April 1st, 1923, together with full particulars regarding the same, no reply to
which has as yet been received.

In order to be in a position to examine, in a satisfactory manner, this part of the revenue of your department, I should
be supplied, at regular intervals, with full particulars of all leases both as regards the terms, of each lease and the
payments that have been received on account thereof. I have accordingly now to request that you furnish me with a list
of all leases in force on April



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 401-404) ===
<!-- page 401 -->
1st, 1924, giving in each case the terms of the lease with the amount due at that date and any payments that may have
been received since, and also full particular with regard to all leases that may have been entered into subsequently.

I have further to request that in future monthly statements be sent this office showing in detail all transactions that
have taken place during the preceding month with regard to leases.

Your obedient servant,
GEORGES GONTHIER, A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, May 18, 1925.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of May 9th on the above subject.

I have pleasure in stating that this Department will co-operate with your officers in carrying out a scheme for the audit
of Indian leases which will be mutually satisfactory.

Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.

The Auditor General.

Indian Trust Fund Revenue: Information desired in connection with Leases on a Crop Share Basis

(Continuation of correspondence on page 1 - 222, Report for 1923 - 24)

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, December 22, 1924.

SIR, - In your letter of May 20th last you requested to be furnished with certain information relative to the issuing of
crop share leases by Commissioner W.M. Graham, of Regina, in connection particularly with certain land sales on the
Blackfoot Indian Reserve. I now have pleasure in supplying you with the desired information.

In a number of cases crop share leases have been granted and approved by this Department on the basis of one-third of
the crop or it's value, being paid to the Department for the purpose of being credited to the sale account. These leases
are subject to careful supervision and an inspector has been employed temporarily for the purpose of checking crop
condition and to see that proper and sufficient return is made to the Department in accordance with the terms of the
lease. Threshing operations, are checked over in order that we may know just what amount of grain has been harvested
and the amount to which the Department is, therefore, properly entitled. The whole crop is marketed by the lessee, and
elevator receipts handed to our official covering the amount of the Department's share. Of course it is not possible for
the Department to

<!-- page 402 -->
receive payment immediately following threshing operations, as it is sometimes advisable to defer settlement for a
short time in order that both the farmer and the Department may benefit from subsequent market fluctuations. It has
not been considered necessary to make provision in crop share leases for the carrying of hail insurance by the lessee.

Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.

The Assistant Auditor General.

Contract: Bersimis combined Day School and Teacher's Residence

AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, September 16, 1925.

SIR, - Let me direct your attention to the payments made to A. Amyot, in connection with the contract for the
construction of a combined day school and teacher's residence on the Bersimis Indian Reserve.

The contract price for this work was $28,980, but extras have been added to the amount of $3,819.07, making the total
payments to the contractor, $32,799.07.

The contract copy sent me states that the contractor agrees to do all the work and provide all the materials of the best
kind shown in the drawings and described in the specifications marked "A" and "B" respectively and signed by the
contractor. These specifications are essential parts of the contract and are necessary for the proper examination of the
accounts.

Other Departments submit progress estimates on contract work to this office for examination and certification prior to
payment, and I am of opinion a similar course should be adopted by your Department.

Has the contractor furnished security for the proper performance of his contract and if so please let me know the
disposition made of such security.

Your obedient servant,
GEORGES GONTHIER, A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, September 23, 1925.

SIR, - I am in receipt of your letter of the 16th instant with reference to the contract work for the Bersimis combined
day school and teachers' residence, completed in August, 1924.

In reply I beg to say that all extras which were awarded to the contractors in connection with this building were in the
nature of additional works not included in the specifications or plan. I am, therefore, sending you as per your request, a
copy of the plan and specifications for verification, under separate cover.

Your obedient servant,
A.P. MACKENZIE,
for Asst. Deputy and Sec'y.

The Auditor General.

<!-- page 403 -->
AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, September 25, 1925.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of the 23rd inst. transmitting specifications for the combined day
school and teacher's residence at Bersimis and stating that none of the extras were included in the specification.

For a proper audit of extra work on a contract, it is essential to know whether these extras were properly authorized by
the architect prior to their performance, or were undertaken by the contractor and authorized at some subsequent date.
Written orders from the architect should be supplied for all extras.

Your letter contains no information regarding the security which should have been furnished nor of the disposition of
that security.

Your obedient servant,
GEORGES GONTHIER, A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, October 1, 1925.

DEAR SIR, - As requested by your letter of the 25th ultimo, I beg to say in connection with the contract for the
erection of the combined day school and teachers' residence at Bersimis, Que., that the necessary security was
furnished by the contractors, and deposited with the Finance Department until the work was fully completed and
satisfactory to the Department.

Yours truly,
F.H. PAGET, Chief Accountant.

The Auditor General.

Grant towards erection of Wing, St. Bruno's Residential School

AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, June 16, 1924.

SIR, - Cheque No. 6370 issued in March last and charged against the vote for Indian Education is for the payment of
$10,775.85 to Rev. C. Falher, O.M.I., as a grant towards the erection of a wing at St. Bruno's Residential School which
was destroyed by fire during the winter of 1923 - 24.

According to the vouchers submitted in support of this payment, your department, with the approval of the
Superintendent General of Indian Affairs offered the Bishop of Athabasca a grant of $12,000 towards the re-building.
The church authorities were to be responsible for the labour on the building and were to present receipted accounts for
the material purchased and for the freighting. The

<!-- page 404 -->
payment in question represents the receipted accounts that have been presented, but a number of the receipted accounts
attached to the vouchers indicate the total amount paid, without giving any particulars as to the quantity and prices of
the materials furnished.

I am of opinion that the authority of the Governor in Council should have been obtained before an expenditure of this
nature was incurred.

Your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, June 24, 1924.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of the 16th instant with reference to the payment
by this Department of a grant toward the erection of a wing at St. Bruno's Boarding School. I have noted for future
reference your opinion that the authority of the Governor in Council should be obtained before expenditures of this
nature are incurred.

Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.

The Assistant Auditor General.


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, June 26, 1924.

SIR, - I am in receipt of your letter of the 24th inst., replying to mine of the 16th with reference to a grant towards the
erection of a wing at St. Bruno's Boarding School.

In your reply you state that you have noted for future reference my opinion that the authority of the Governor in
Council should be obtained before expenditures of this nature are incurred.

While my previous letter did not so definitely state, still it was intended to express my opinion, not only that all future
payments of a like nature should be authorized by the Governor in Council, but all that such authority should be
obtained for the particular payment in question. I have accordingly to request that you take the necessary steps to
obtain the approval of the Governor in Council to this grant to St. Bruno's School.


Your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.
